item.title: Next Michigan AD: 'It depends' on coach-student sexual relationships
item.description: Trev Alberts , who is expected to be named the University of Michigan's next athletic director, said "it depends" when asked during a December deposition whether college coaches should ever have sexual relationships with student-athletes , despite a University of Nebraska-Lincoln policy prohibiting such relationships. Alberts gave the testimony during the deposition as a defendant in an ongoing federal lawsuit alleging that he and other University of Nebraska-Lincoln officials mishandled a sexual relationship between an associate women's basketball coach and a player during his tenure as athletic director. The lawsuit was filed by Ashley Scoggin, a former Nebraska women's basketball player. She claimed the university didn't protect her and failed to properly investigate how she, as a student-athlete, was "groomed" by associate women's basketball coach Chuck Love to carry on a secret relationship. Alberts is named as a defendant, along with head coach Amy Williams, Love and Nebraska's Board of Regents. In a response to Scoggin's lawsuit, attorneys for Williams, Alberts and the university denied her allegations and said the defendants were unaware of the details of the relationship until she filed a Title IX complaint in March 2022. The lawsuit also alleges Alberts failed to question Williams' decision to remove Scoggin from the team or investigate whether Love had relationships with other students and whether Williams knew about them. It further alleges he failed to require employee training or clarify athletic department policies prohibiting sexual relationships between coaches and student-athletes. The lawsuit also alleges Alberts encouraged Scoggin to leave Nebraska and allowed Love to resign voluntarily. Attorneys for Scoggin declined to comment. Messages were left with Alberts and attorneys for him and the university. Nebraska's Senior Director of Communications Cara Pesek declined to comment and said the university did not comment on pending litigation. More: Trev Alberts set to become next UM athletic director Expert questions Alberts' comments as Michigan faces scrutiny Nellie Drew, the director of the Center for the Advancement of Sport at the University at Buffalo School of Law, said Alberts' comments were "flabbergasting." Understanding the university's and federal government's policies regarding Title IX and sexual harassment are a "core component" of an athletic director's job, she said. "There's a difference between not being aware of something happening and not being aware of what you need to be doing as a mandatory reporter," Drew said. "He was (at the Nebraska system) for a long time, should’ve been doing mandatory training. ... He signs off on annual affirmations that the university is in compliance." Alberts' answers to two depositions from December and February were first reported by David Covucci of FOIAball . item.title: Philadelphia Eagles Finally Get Good News Before Steelers Game
item.description: It has been an absolutely miserable NFL season for the Philadelphia Eagles, and at no point have things been looking up. The Eagles are just 2-7 heading into their Week 11 matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jalen Hurts is out for the season. They traded multiple key pieces before the trade deadline. Their receiving corps have also been riddled with injuries. But in terms of the latter, Philadelphia has finally received some good news. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks were in practice this week, and Smith particular has been given the green light to play this Sunday against the Steelers, per the team’s injury report . Smith last played on Oct. 18 due to a hamstring injury. In the four games he has played this season, he has logged 26 catches for 310 yards and a couple of touchdowns. Where do the Philadelphia Eagles go from here? Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (6) walks off the field after a loss against the Carolina Panthers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Eagles appear to be entering a rebuilding phase, and their future is definitely up in the air. On the bright side, Philadelphia has stockpiled draft capital thanks to the recent trades it has made. Philly moved center Cam Jurgens and defensive tackle Jordan Davis prior to the deadline. And last June, it sent wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots. That obviously puts the Eagles in a strong position moving forward, especially with general manager Howie Roseman at the helm. But with Hurts’ future very much uncertain due to blood clots, Philadelphia may have to consider making a change under center in the spring, so it will be interesting to see how the Eagles approach it. For now, though, there is now question that Philadelphia is no longer a legitimate contender and will definitely have to retool in order to re-establish itself as a serious threat in the NFC East. item.title: Vikings Receive Sudden Injury News Before 49ers Game
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings have been dealing with a whole lot of injury issues recently, and now, another problem has surfaced before their Week 11 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers. Vikings cornerback Isaiah Rodgers, who has developed into a crucial part of the team’s secondary, is now questionable to play this Sunday as a result of a calf injury that limited him in practice both Thursday and Friday. The development was revealed by Minnesota head coach Kevin O’Connell while speaking to reporters on Friday. O’Connell certainly didn’t seem overly pessimistic, but Rodgers’ condition is obviously something to monitor heading into the Vikings’ showdown in Mexico City. “He was limited today. It felt pretty good,” O’Connell said . “We’ll see how he feels post-practice treatment and all that.” Minnesota Vikings can send another strong message Dec 25, 2025; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell looks on in the second quarter against the Detroit Lions at U.S. Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Krohn-Imagn Images The Vikings looked fantastic during Kirk Cousins’ debut against the Green Bay Packers last Sunday, coming away with a 30-10 win at Lambeau Field and completing a regular-season sweep of their NFC North rivals. Now, Minnesota will have a chance to send another strong message this weekend. The 49ers are 8-1 and are obvious Super Bowl contenders, so this matchup could potentially represent an NFC Championship Game preview. If the Vikings are able to come away with another win, their title hopes will be taken that much more seriously. Minnesota acquired Cousins before the NFL trade deadline, bringing him back for his second stint in the Twin Cities. He initially played for the Vikings between 2018 and 2023, but failed to lead the Vikings to a Super Bowl appearance. That could certainly change this year, as Minnesota boasts a dominant defense and a plethora of weapons offensively. A victory over San Francisco would go a long way in proving that the Vikings are, in fact, for real. item.title: Bayern provide injury update on Olise after French star leaves stadium on crutches
item.description: Bayern provide injury update on Olise after French star leaves stadium on crutches While Harry Kane is set to be sidelined for several months after suffering a syndesmosis tear in Friday's 1-1 draw with 1. item.title: Can No. 10 Cougars finally solve the Kansas riddle?
item.description: BYU Cougars head coach Kalani Sitake walks the sideline during game against the Baylor Bears, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, at LaVell Edwards Stadium in Provo. | Erin Hooley, Deseret News LAWRENCE, Kansas — Sunny skies and unseasonably warm temperatures have greeted residents in this college town some 35 miles west of Kansas City all week, but at least some of that is expected to end Saturday when the No. 10 BYU Cougars invade “The Booth” — otherwise known as David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium. Cloudier conditions, cooler temperatures and perhaps a light drizzle early turning into a 55% chance of thunderstorms in the afternoon could ruin the string of perfect days in the northeast quadrant of the Sunflower State, just as the surging Jayhawks attempt to wreck the Cougars’ hopes of making it to the College Football Playoff and/or the Big 12 championship game. Kickoff is at 10 a.m. MST and the pivotal Big 12 game will be televised nationally by ABC. Going off the teams’ records, it would appear that BYU (8-2, 5-2) should be a heavy favorite over somewhat disappointing Kansas (4-6, 2-5), until one takes a closer look at the Jayhawks’ talent level, performance against other top Big 12 teams, and history against the Cougars. For instance, the Jayhawks are 3-0 all-time against BYU, 2-0 in Big 12 games, and are the only team in the entire conference that the Cougars have never defeated. In BYU’s first-ever Big 12 game, Kansas got two defensive touchdowns and a big game from Jalon Daniels to edge the Cougars 38-27 in front of 47,233 in Lawrence. Two years later, the Jayhawks ruined undefeated BYU’s perfect season with a 17-13 upset in Provo, a devastating setback for the then-No. 6 Cougars that kept them out of the CFP and the Big 12 championship game. “I remember it was a rough start (in 2023),” BYU coach Kalani Sitake said Monday. “I liked our start this past week against Baylor better. So, it was a rough start. It’s not easy to go out on the road, especially in conference games. We know we have to have our minds right, and make sure that everybody is clicking.” One particular player that needs to be clicking for the Cougars is senior running back LJ Martin , who is creeping closer to full strength after having played sparingly the past two games — the 28-20 loss at No. 2 Utah and the 28-7 victory over the Bears last week at LaVell Edwards Stadium. “They’ve competed with every single team they’ve played. This is the best 4-6 team I’ve ever seen (with) the type of talent they have on their offense. It’s very impressive.” BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga on the Kansas Jayhawks “I just know that he gets a little better each day and each week and (Tuesday) was the best he’s looked since he’s been back,” BYU offensive coordinator Aaron Roderick said. “So I wouldn’t say he’s 100% yet, but he looked good.” Quarterback Bear Bachmeier has been forced to carry more than his share of the load in Martin’s absence, but on Monday he said he’s “feeling good” physi

item.title: Greinke And Hosmer Join Royals Hall Of Fame For 2027 Class
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images The Kansas City Royals have chosen two familiar faces for their 2027 Hall of Fame class. The team made the announcement to mark their lasting impact on the franchise. In the 2002 MLB Draft, Greinke was selected sixth overall. He made his debut in 2004 and pitched for the team until 2010. After a long career with other teams, he returned for his final two seasons in 2022 and 2023. His time in Kansas City included a Cy Young Award win in 2009, according to Royals Keep . He remains the most recent Royals pitcher to earn that title. A Pitcher’s Legacy in the Majors Greinke’s stats show his value to the team over many years. He ranks fourth in club history for strikeouts and sixth in starts. During his career, he earned six All-Star appearances and six Gold Glove Awards. He also won two Silver Slugger Awards while playing for the Dodgers, Angels, Astros and Diamondbacks. His return to the rotation in 2022 helped close out his career in the city where it began. The 2009 season stands out as a peak moment for the franchise. Greinke became the third Royals pitcher to win the Cy Young Award. David Cone won it in 1994 and Bret Saberhagen won it in 1985 and 1989. His ability to dominate hitters made him a key figure for years. Hosmer and the World Series Win Hosmer was the third overall pick in the 2008 draft. He debuted in 2011 and spent his first seven years in Kansas City. His defense at first base earned him four Gold Glove awards. He also won an All-Star Game MVP in 2016 and a Silver Slugger Award in 2017. The 2015 World Series remains the crowning achievement of his time with the Royals. Hosmer played a vital part in the team’s title run against the New York Mets. He scored the game-tying run in the clinching game to propel the team to victory. The game-tying run helped the Royals win their first championship since 1985. His contribution was instrumental in securing the trophy. Despite playing elsewhere, his roots in Kansas City run deep. The team recognized his role in the 2014 and 2015 World Series appearances. His legacy includes the excitement of those playoff runs. Induction Marks a New Chapter The announcement came from the team with a clear statement of pride. “We are proud to announce the newest inductees into the Royals Hall of Fame, Zack Greinke and Eric Hosmer!” the Kansas City Royals said. Greinke and Hosmer each played significant roles in Royals history. Their careers spanned the team’s pitching peak and its championship glory. Royals fans hold the two forever indebted in their hearts. The 2027 class will join the ranks of legends who shaped the game in Kansas City.

item.title: NCAA women's soccer tournament schedule 2026: TV channels, times, live streams, scores for every college game
item.description: NCAA women's soccer tournament schedule 2026: TV channels, times, live streams, scores for every college game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The NCAA women's soccer tournament is back, with a blend of familiar powers and emerging programs set to strive for a national championship. While the regular season indicates there should be several legitimate contenders to lift the trophy in Cary, North Carolina, there is one safe bet entering the tournament: The ACC will play a prominent role. At least one ACC team has appeared in the championship game each of the last eight years, with a conference team bringing home the national title each of the last three years. Florida State took the 2025 and 2023 crowns, but the Seminoles have looked mortal this year as the sport's most decorated program has reemerged. North Carolina, which won its 22nd national championship two years ago, looks like the team to beat once again after taking the ACC title. There will be challengers, though. Vanderbilt suffered its first loss of the season in the SEC quarterfinals and is looking for its first NCAA title, along with a trio of Big Ten teams in Purdue, Michigan State and Ohio State. Who will emerge from the 64-team field? Here's all you need to know to watch every game. item.title: Mike Pettine will call an aggressive Dallas Cowboys defense that impacts the quarterback
item.description: Mike Pettine says he has gained a lot of respect for Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker for how he has handled getting play calling duties take away from him. Pettine, the team's senior defensive assistant, will call plays on defense for the rest of the season. Mike Pettine didn’t expect to be the defensive play caller when he came out of retirement last month and joined the Dallas Cowboys as a senior defensive assistant to help defensive coordinator Christian Parker, his overwhelmed 34-year-old former protege. “It certainly wasn’t the intention,” Pettine said on Friday, the first day he talked to the media since being named the defensive play caller on Wednesday in hopes of turning around a defense that ranks last in the in league yards, rushing yards and third-down perception and hopefully reviving a disappointing Cowboys season (4-6), starting in Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans (1-8). “There no seed of this panted at any point. This business is week to week and sometimes circumstances happen and change has to be made.” He also doesn’t know if he will back in the same role or serve as Cowboys defensive coordinator next season. He has to check with his wife and see what she says about all that. “I have to check with my wife on that one,” Pettine said. “We’re week to week and see what plays out.” Make no mistake about, Pettine, 60, is still a football coach and loves what he is doing. He has been all on on the job since he got into building after the Cowboys had to talk him out of retirement while he was vacationing in Italy with his wife. “Sometimes, circumstances happen where they build up where changes has to be made,” Pettine said. “That’s what happening. Our focus is we’re full speed ahead. Not going to take time and look in the rear view mirror, woulda, coulda, shoulda. We’re all about getting ourselves right and preparing for the Titans.” Even tough he has a close relationship with Parker _ he gave him his first job in in 2019 when he was defensive coordinator with the Green Bay Packers _ Pettine said he didn’t hesitate when head coach Brian Schottenheimer asked him to take over as the play caller. “I know having been in Schotty’s chair before that he’s got to make a tough decision,” Pettine said. “When you’re part of a team, it’s a bottom-line business. So as difficult as it is to see a friend go through that and have this happen to them, clearly a step backwards, no. I just knew it wouldn’t be that awkward or that difficult because of him and how he would handle it, and because of the strength of our relationship. Our relationship is way stronger, way more important than who’s calling plays on Sunday.” Pettine said Parker has handled the situation as well as can be expected. Parker said this was a significant personal setback and thought about quitting all together. Pettine was hired as a consultant because of the early season struggles of the unit. Now, he’s here to save the day. “It was a tough stretch for

item.title: NBA Moves Cavs-Heat Game To 3 PM For Browns Flex
item.description: Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images The NBA made a big change to the schedule for Sunday, Nov. 29. The game between the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Miami Heat will now start at 3:00 PM EST, according to Fear The Sword . It was set to begin at 6:00 PM before this shift. The league did not give a specific reason for the move. However, the change lines up perfectly with the Cleveland Browns’ Sunday Night Football game against the Las Vegas Raiders. That football game was flexed to 8:30 PM on NBC. This timing lets fans in the city watch both pro sports teams on the same day. It is a rare chance to see two home games in one weekend. This is the second time these two teams will face off this season. The first matchup happened on Nov. 13. The Heat won that game by a score of 133-121. Miami was strong without Evan Mobley playing for Cleveland. Donovan Mitchell led the Cavs with 25 points in that loss. But the defense was the main problem for Cleveland that night. Both Bam Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 37 points for Miami. The Heat are riding a six-game winning streak right now. They started the season cold but have found their rhythm. Heat Momentum and Coaching Frustration Miami looks dangerous as they enter this new schedule. They beat the Milwaukee Bucks 137-130 on Nov. 18. With 27 points, 14 rebounds, and nine assists, Giannis Antetokounmpo ruled that victory. He did not make a single three-pointer in that game. Bam Adebayo added 26 points. The team shot 22 three-pointers total. This offensive fire makes them a tough test for the Cavs. Yet, the Heat coach is not happy with how the league runs the game. Erik Spoelstra called the current challenge rules a “clown show.” He thinks the rules hurt the flow of basketball. Spoelstra wants his stars to play without worrying about stopping the clock for reviews. The rules let coaches challenge two plays per game. If the first one fails, they lose the right to challenge again. If it works, they get a second one later. Spoelstra says this stops the game from moving. Referees take as much time for a review as they do for a timeout. This makes games run long and frustrates fans. Spoelstra wants his team to focus on basketball, not on replay reviews. He knows the league wants to get calls right, but he thinks the cost is too high. The flow of the game changes too much when the clock stops. Cleveland Needs to Fix Its Defense The Cavs have had their own struggles this season. They lost to the Heat badly in their last meeting. Cleveland has dealt with injuries and defensive lapses. They beat the Minnesota Timberwolves and the New York Knicks recently. Those were good wins, but the defense still needs work. The team is jockeying for position in the Eastern Conference. Both teams are close in the standings. The Heat have won six straight. The Cavs have had ups and downs. This game at 3 PM is a key test for both sides. Miami wants to keep their streak alive. item.title: Detroit Tigers Lock Up Troy Melton With Long-Term Extension
item.description: The Detroit Tigers have made a significant investment in their future, and one of their most promising young pitchers isn’t going anywhere anytime soon. According to ESPN’s Jeff Passan , the Tigers have agreed to a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension with right-handed pitcher Troy Melton , keeping him under contract through the 2032 season. The deal also includes a club option for 2033, potentially keeping Melton in Detroit through his age-32 season. And here’s where things get even more interesting. According to MLB.com’s Mark Feinsand , the contract could reach $80 million with incentives , giving Melton an opportunity to earn considerably more if he continues developing into a frontline starter. The Tigers have not yet officially announced the agreement, but the reported terms represent one of Scott Harris’ biggest investments in a young pitcher since taking over Detroit’s baseball operations. Sep 1, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Detroit Tigers starting pitcher Troy Melton (52) delivers a pitch against the Minnesota Twins in the first inning at Target Field. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Troy Melton Earns Massive Extension After Breakout 2026 Season Melton, 25, proved himself as one of Detroit’s most valuable pitchers during the 2026 season after transitioning into a full-time starting role. The right-hander made 20 starts and posted an impressive 2.76 ERA over 114⅓ innings , striking out 94 batters while walking 37. His 152 ERA+ meant he performed 52 percent better than the league average after adjusting for ballpark factors, an impressive accomplishment for a pitcher in his first full season primarily working as a starter. Melton also recorded a 1.13 WHIP, demonstrating his ability to limit opposing hitters while working deeper into games. Those numbers were particularly encouraging considering he began the season on the injured list with right elbow inflammation. Originally selected by Detroit in the fourth round of the 2022 MLB Draft out of San Diego State, Melton made his Major League debut in 2025 and quickly established himself as an important part of the organization’s pitching plans. Now, Detroit is rewarding that progress with a substantial financial commitment. Scott Harris Locks Up Another Piece of Tigers’ Future Perhaps the most significant aspect of the agreement is the timing. Melton wasn’t even scheduled to become arbitration-eligible until 2029, meaning Detroit could have retained him on a series of relatively inexpensive contracts before eventually facing larger salary decisions. Instead, Harris and the Tigers have decided to secure cost certainty now rather than waiting for Melton’s price to potentially climb. The reported $46.5 million guarantee works out to an average of $7.75 million per season , a potentially valuable figure if Melton develops into a consistent top-of-the-rotation starter. item.title: Dianna Russini tell-all book reportedly in the works
item.description: Credit: 98.5 The Sports Hub Dianna Russini returned to the sports media world but has been noticeably mum about her controversial relationship with Mike Vrabel and the professional and personal fallout from that scandal. That might be because she’s saving it for a tell-all book. During Friday’s episode of Felger & Mazz on Boston’s 98.5 The Sports Hub, co-host “Big” Jim Murray dropped a bit of news while discussing the New England Patriots head coach’s struggles this season. “I have a little nugget for you,” Murray offered as a tease to Felger & Mazz’s Michael Felger and Tony Massarotti. “You remember Teddy Atlas, the boxing commentator? He has an annual event around Thanksgiving. It was held last night in New York, and she was there. And a friend of mine was chatting with Dianna Russini, and she’s got a book coming out. So, and she said she’ll be talking about everything that’s gone on, is what she told my friend. “She’s come out with this podcast. It’s been one big nothing these last couple of weeks. Maybe [Mike Vrabel] knows that a book is coming that’s going to— she’s going to further expound on this whole situation.” According to 98.5 The Sports Hub’s “Big” Jim Murray, Dianna Russini is telling people she has a tell-all book in the works. “She said she’ll be talking about everything that’s gone on, is what she told my friend.” https://t.co/wc6srhoXZt — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 20, 2026 Just in case you don’t want to take Murray’s word for it, here’s proof that Russini was indeed at the 30th Annual Teddy Dinner, hosted by the Dr. Theodore A. Atlas Foundation, at the Hilton Garden Inn in Staten Island, New York. It has long been suggested that Russini would want to write a tell-all book in order to tell her side of the story. Aside from denying that she had done anything untoward in her resignation from The Athletic , Russini made few public comments during the scandal. Right before she returned with BetUS’s The Russini Report last week , she told People that “ the lies became so out of control ,” but did not offer details on what those lies were. While her BetUS show has stuck to NFL news and interviews, her upcoming podcast with Stugotz might be a platform where she offers more insight into her feelings and thoughts on the scandal that severely damaged her reputation as an NFL reporter. For his part, Vrabel’s playbook was to vaguely apologize for “something” and try to move forward , which has largely worked so far . However, Russini’s desire to come clean or tell her side of the story has always been his wild card. Depending on what she has to say about her relationship with Vrabel and whatever else he might have said or done, the Patriots’ head coach might not be out of the woods yet. At the very least, he might need to attend a second counseling session . The post Dianna Russini tell-all book in the works, per 98.5 The Sports Hub’s Jim Murray appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Mets tender Mark Vientos to give slugger another shot
item.description: Mark Vientos didn't adapt well to playing first base, but his raw power may still compel the Mets to tender him a contract. The Mets are giving things another go with one of their up-and-down homegrown pieces. Mark Vientos was tendered a contract ahead of Friday’s 5 p.m. deadline as the Mets made their initial internal roster decisions for 2027. Vientos hit 13 homers with just a .652 OPS over 87 games — dealing with a right hand fracture over the summer — with a minus-1.2 WAR, according to Baseball Reference. Mark Vientos has been tendered a contract for 2027. JASON SZENES FOR THE NEW YORK POST But even with the lack of thump and inconsistent defense at first base, Vientos, 26, will get another crack with the Mets. In other moves, the Mets nontendered pitcher Dylan Ross, catcher Hayden Senger and infielder Christopher Morel. The team also claimed righty pitchers Gus Varland (Nationals) and Yunior Tur (A’s) off waivers.

item.title: Price survives match darts to reach Grand Slam semis
item.description: Gerwyn Price won the last of his three Grand Slam of Darts titles in 2021 [Getty Images] Gerwyn Price faced two match darts before winning a thrilling quarter-final against Nico Springer at the Grand Slam of Darts, as Luke Littler's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena was knocked out. Three-time champion Price led for most of the match but his German opponent refused to let him out of reach. Springer missed a number of chances to level, including three darts at double top to make it 13-13 as he fell 14-12 behind, before he eventually made it 14-14 and then took a 15-14 lead. However, Price produced a stunning 143 checkout to take it to a decider in which Springer had the throw. The German left himself 73 after his 16th 180, only to miss double eight and double four for the match prior to Price taking out 78 with treble 18 and double 12. "I'm quite lucky to come through that game," Price told Sky Sports. "I missed so many chances - I should've punished him. "I kept him in the game, I kept missing doubles after doubles. Even though he was scoring as well as I was, I was missing opportunities after opportunities but I'm glad I had another one at the end." Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money Price will play Kevin Doets in the semi-finals after the Dutchman beat compatriot Wattimena, who beat world number one and world champion Littler in the second round. Doets was 5-4 down before taking a dominant hold of the match with a remarkable 10-leg burst. He hit two 170 checkouts as he surged into a 14-5 lead before Wattimena managed to temporarily halt him by taking the 20th leg. However, Doets quickly went on to wrap up victory as he finished off the 23rd leg with a 180 - his eighth of the match - and double 18. "The beginning was very tight but, after the 5-5, I just felt like I was walking away with it," said Doets. When talking about his 170 finishes, he added: "It's amazing to do that - it feels really good to do that." Saturday's quarter-finals will involve Gian van Veen playing Nathan Aspinall and Michael van Gerwen facing Tom Sykes, who beat Luke Humphries. Follow live text coverage on the semi-finals (13:00 GMT) and final (19:30) on the BBC Sport website and app on Sunday, 22 November. item.title: ‘I think that’s very clear this year’: Nick Saban insists SEC is better than Big Ten despite title drought
item.description: Nick Saban is on stage at ESPN College GameDay ahead of the University of Oklahoma-Michigan College football game on Sep 6, 2025 in Norman. The Big Ten has won three straight national championships, but the SEC has been getting most of the love from the College Football Playoff selection committee this season. That has sparked plenty of debate about which conference is really the best in college football. On Friday, former Alabama head coach Nick Saban weighed in, arguing that winning a national title doesn’t mean that a conference is the strongest. Saban, who spent more than two decades coaching in the SEC at LSU and Alabama, said the league’s strength “from top to bottom” has always set it apart, and that it’s “very clear this year.” SEC Dominating CFP Rankings The SEC hasn’t won a national championship since Georgia went back-to-back in the 2021 and 2022 seasons. Since then, Michigan, Ohio State, and Indiana have all brought the title back to the Big Ten, with Indiana completing an undefeated 16-0 season by beating Miami 27-21 in January. But the SEC has nine teams in this week’s College Football Playoff rankings, including No. 1 Georgia, No. 3 Alabama, No. 5 Texas, and No. 9 Tennessee. Four-loss South Carolina, Oklahoma, Florida, and Ole Miss are also ranked between No. 21 and No. 25. According to an analysis by Brandon Marcello of CBS Sports, the committee has ranked SEC teams a combined 41 spots higher than the AP poll through its first three rankings, the biggest edge any conference has had since 2014. The Big Ten, meanwhile, has never fared worse. The rankings have drawn plenty of criticism, including from Fox Sports analyst Joel Klatt, who said this week that it’s time to “ take the crayons away from the committee .” Saban, of course, has been banging the drum for the SEC all season. Back in September, he called the Big Ten “ three good teams at the top and then nothing .” ‘From top to bottom’ Saban addressed the SEC and Big Ten debate during Friday’s episode of The Pat McAfee Show . “Just because you win a national championship does not make and evaluate the level of your league. It means you had a really, really good team that was better than everybody else, but it doesn’t mean you necessarily had the best league from top to bottom. My argument with the SEC has always been the strength of the league, from top to bottom. I think that’s very clear this year, in terms of how many good teams there are,” Saban said, via The Pat McAfee Show . Saban also acknowledged that the SEC’s depth might not be the best thing for the league when it comes to the playoff. “But it’s always been that way and they beat up on each other, and that’s not necessarily the best thing for this 12-team playoff. I get it. I mean, I understand the Big Ten won three championships in a row. That means they had the best team three years in a row. It doesn’t necessarily mean they had the best league from top to bottom,” Saban continued. It’s worth noting that the committe

item.title: Giants shocked to learn Colts cut ex-teammate Daniel Jones
item.description: Daniel Jones has been released by the Colts. John Harbaugh’s eyes nearly popped out of his head upon learning that the Colts cut quarterback Daniel Jones . Harbaugh wasn’t the Giants’ head coach when they stunningly cut Jones in November 2024, so they don’t have the personal relationship that Jones maintains with others in East Rutherford. But the Colts are next week’s opponent, so the Giants’ behind-the-scenes advance-scouting staffers were just thrown a major curveball. The Colts plan to start first-round draft bust Anthony Richardson , which means an offense that could be more option-based in store on Nov. 29 to hide Richardson’s passing inaccuracy. Daniel Jones has been released by the Colts. Getty Images “[It changes] probably pretty dramatically. I mean, wow,’” Harbaugh admitted. “I don’t want to get ahead of ourselves here, and you just hit me with that. But definitely the offense will be the offense that they run, but it’ll be centered around the quarterback for sure, and they’re probably different styles to some degree, so we’ll have to look at that when the time comes. We have people doing that this week. They’ll have to make a left turn, obviously.” Unlike when the Giants demoted Jones from starter to third-stringer to protect themselves against an injury clause in his contract, Jones did not ask the Colts for his release, head coach Shane Steichen said. In the Giants locker room, news of Jones’ release brought back memories. What does it say to teammates when you release the quarterback who started the first 11 games? “That the writing is on the wall for the season and you have to get through the next six games the best you can play,” right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor told The Post. “D.J. is a great guy but he’s in such a predicament. He went there last year and balled out, so it’s definitely not a ‘him’ thing. When you trade everyone like they did, it’s hard.” John Harbaugh, head coach of the Giants. Getty Images Giants backup offensive lineman Josh Sills was with the Colts last season and to start 2025. He saw the same hard-working Jones that was beloved by Giants teammates. “He helped me in any and every way imaginable,” Sills told The Post. “He went above and beyond to make sure everyone had what they needed to achieve their goals. It’s a team game. It takes 11 guys.” Anthony Richardson will now start at quarterback for the Colts. Getty Images Next week was billed as the Jones Revenge Game. Instead, Jones didn’t even make it through the first year of the two-year, $88 million contract that he signed after a torn Achilles. Jones might be able to help the Patriots or Ravens in their playoff chase. Or he could help the Eagles not be an embarrassment the rest of the season. Or use his ties to Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb to become the backup for a Super Bowl contender. item.title: Tigers, Troy Melton agree to $46.5 million contract extension
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tigers, Troy Melton agree to $46.5 million contract extension appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Tigers probably won’t be able to bring Tarik Skubal back this offseason (although anything is possible), but they made a significant move on Friday nonetheless. According to Jeff Passan of ESPN, Detroit and starting pitcher Troy Melton are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension. “BREAKING: Right-hander Troy Melton and the Detroit Tigers are in agreement on a six-year, $46.5 million contract extension, sources tell ESPN. Deal includes a club option for 2033 and can max out at $80 million. Big payday for the 25-year-old with 160 career major league innings,” Passan reported. The Tigers have been willing to add players through free agency this offseason. However, they clearly have a desire to extend some of their younger players on the roster. Detroit is looking to build around a core of players in hopes of developing a legitimate contender soon. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Melton, who is only 25 years old as Passan mentioned, has appeared in 36 total big league games in his career. He made 16 appearances (four starts) in 2025 and 20 starts in 2026. Overall, he has recorded a 2.76 ERA across his 36 career outings. item.title: ‘It will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has shown here’ — Bayern Munich legend unsure if Jamal Musiala can reach previous heights
item.description: (Photo by Adam Pretty/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jamal Musiala is finally back on the pitch for Bayern Munich after nearly two months on the sidelines, but there are still some significant questions about what comes next for the German international. Musiala recently made his return, logging approximately 20 minutes of playing tim e against 1. FC Köln. While getting him back into action is certainly encouraging, former Bayern Munich CEO and current supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge is not ready to draw any conclusions about the attacking midfielder’s performance or future just yet. Speaking about Musiala ‘s return and the comments previously made by honorary president Uli Hoeneß and CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, Rummenigge defended the club’s approach to the situation. “Well, I don’t think you can properly assess any footballer based on 20 minutes. I know what you’re getting at, but I don’t see anything controversial about it at all. What Uli said, and what Jan Dreesen also said yesterday, is perfectly reasonable in my view. He has a health-related issue, and that’s well known. It’s also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that’s responsible and perfectly normal,” said Rummenigge (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). That is an interesting way of framing things. Musial a is one of Bayern’s most important players when healthy, but his injury situation and enormous financial commitment mean the club has legitimate r easons to c onsider the bigger picture. Bayern needs Musiala back to his best, but the club also needs to be realistic about the risks and expectations involved. Unfortunately, Rummenigge’s next comments were considerably less encouraging. Asked whether he shared Hoeneß’s concerns that Musiala might never return to his previous level, Rummenigge acknowledged that possibility. “That is certainly possible and cannot be ruled out. Quite simply, what we know unfortunately suggests that it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has shown here in this stadium on so many occasions,” Rummenigge stated (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). That is a sobering assessment from someone who knows Bayern Munich exceptionally well. Nobody should expect Musiala to immed iately rediscover his best form after an extended absence this season, his summer injury, or even the maj or leg injury he sustained at the Club World Cup in 2025 — the Germany international still needs time. It gets even more complex when considering Musiala’s ongoing management of absence seizures caused by a neurological condition, which appears to be under control at the moment. Rummenigge’s comments suggest that Bayern Munich’s concerns extend beyond simply getting the 23-year-old back into the lineup. There are legitimate questions about wheth er he can fully recover the explosiveness, confidence, and individual brilliance that made him such a devastating att

item.title: Dodgers reportedly trade for Twins .731 OPS infielder and No. 1 overall pick
item.description: Dodgers reportedly trade for Twins .731 OPS infielder and No. 1 overall pick originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Dodgers have an incredible roster already, and there's not really much that this team needs to add this offseason. But, that doesn't mean they're not going to make moves. This offseason, the Dodgers could look for some infield help, and that's exactly the move they've reportedly just made a week before Thanksgiving. According to Jon Heyman of The New York Post , the Dodgers are acquiring Royce Lewis, the former No. 1 overall pick and a career .731 OPS infielder from the Minnesota Twins in a surprise trade. Dodgers reportedly acquire Royce Lewis from Twins "Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers," Heyman reported Friday afternoon. The move for the Dodgers is not yet official, but it's a fascinating addition for Los Angeles this offseason. With Miguel Rojas retiring this offseason, the Dodgers needed a versatile infielder who is also a right-handed hitter. That's exactly what Lewis is, and he's now on his way to Los Angeles. Lewis, the 27-year-old former No. 1 overall pick back in the 2017 MLB Draft, is coming off his fifth season playing in the Majors, all with the Twins. He's struggled to stay healthy in his MLB career, playing at most 125 games in a season, which came this past year with the Twins. MORE : MLB Hot Stove tracker: Live updates on news, rumors, signings and trades for 2026 free agency In his 383-game career in the Majors so far, Lewis has posted 4.9 bWAR with a .731 OPS, 61 homers, 341 hits, 168 runs scored, 69 doubles, one triple, and 213 RBI. He's also set to receive a decent arbitration deal, potentially around $5 million for 2027, and is under club control through the 2028 MLB season. According to Heyman , the Dodgers are sending the Twins catching prospect Francisco Espinoza to complete this trade. Los Angeles is getting some infield help, while the Twins move on from a disappointing No. 1 overall pick a decade after making the selection. Royce Lewis is coming to Los Angeles this offseason, giving the Dodgers an intriguing high-upside right-handed hitting infielder who can play third base, second base, and first base, while providing some pop in the lineup. item.title: Eagles Get Back Star Wide Receiver vs. Steelers
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver Devonta Smith during a game against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Dec. 15, 2024. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Philadelphia Eagles wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring) is set to return against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Smith, who’s missed the last three games, does not have an injury designation for the game. Getting Smith back could provide a big boost for an ailing Eagles team. Smith has caught 26 passes for 310 yards (11.9 average) and two touchdowns in four games this year. In 2025, he recorded 77 receptions for 1,008 yards and four touchdowns. Smith had a big game in the Eagles’ Week 15 win over the Steelers in 2024, recording 11 receptions on 12 targets for 109 yards (9.9 average) and one touchdown. That, of course, was with Jalen Hurts at quarterback, however. Hurts is out for the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. Tanner McKee lost all three starts after Hurts was sidelined. He was benched for Joe Milton leading up to the game against the New York Giants in Week 9. The Eagles signed Milton off the Dallas Cowboys’ practice squad on Oct. 16. Milton completed 18 of 34 passes (52.9%) for 169 yards with no touchdowns, one interception, and a passer rating of 66.9 in the Eagles’ 19-11 loss to New York. He also rushed for 69 yards on seven carries (7.1 average). Sunday will be Milton’s second career start. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) continues to practice as he eyes a return Sunday against the Steelers. pic.twitter.com/WTiCZJTIsA — Olivia Reiner (@ReinerOlivia) November 20, 2026 The Eagles have lost seven straight after starting the season 2-0. It’s the first time since 1999 that the Eagles have started 2-7. The Eagles had a bye in Week 11, so they had extra time to prepare for the Steelers. Nick Sirianni is 5-0 when coming off a bye in his career as the Eagles’ head coach. Eagles wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) and linebacker Zack Baun (back) have both been ruled out for Sunday. item.title: Guardians Non-Tender David Fry, Reach Deals with Festa, Perkins and Holderman
item.description: CLEVELAND, OH - OCTOBER 18: Shin-Soo Choo poses for a photo with David Fry #6 of the Cleveland Guardians after delivering the ceremonial first pitch prior to Game Five of the American League Championship Series between the Tampa Bay Rays and the Cleveland Guardians at Progressive Field on Sunday, October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The Guardians have let go of David Fry, reached 2027 deals with Matt Festa, Blake Perkins and Colin Holderman, and tendered contracts to their remaining arbitration-eligible players. The move to let Fry go is not a surprise but indicates a belief in Kody Huff and perhaps a willingness to pursue an upgrade in righr-handed power in free agency. The move to retain Perkins on what is surely a relatively small amount of money is surprising to me. Perkins, when healthy, has been an excellent centerfielder and has a 95 wRC+ against LHP and has an optiin remaining. Is it possible they see him and Petey Halpin as a workable platoon in center? I hope not. The Guardians may still DFA Perkins should they need the roster spot and try to get him through waivers. Meanwhile, Festa and Holderman have show themselves to be good to great options in the bullpen. I am glad to see both retained, especially Holderman whom I’m pretty (irrationally) convinced would have won us a pennant if healthy. Usually, they’d reach deals with arbitration-eligible players like Steven Kwan, Jo Adell, Gavin Williams, Cade Smith, Tim Herrin and Patrick Bailey in January, but with the lockout looming, expect that to hurriedly occur in April at the earliest. Now, to see if the Guardians do anything else before December 1st when the lockout will be instituted by MLB owners to try to force a salary cap and floor.

item.title: NFL great Brady could buy Chelsea stake
item.description: Tom Brady is a seven-time Super Bowl champion [Getty Images] American football great Tom Brady is looking to invest in Chelsea through ownership group Clearlake Capital. The seven-time Super Bowl winner has recently divested his stake in Championship club Birmingham City, which he bought into following Tom Wagner's Knighthead Capital takeover in 2023. It now appears he could move into Chelsea, where he has a positive relationship with influential co-owner Behdad Eghbali, having been a star guest at the after-party following the club's Club World Cup triumph in 2025. Brady would have no voting rights or control at Chelsea, although the ownership group could look to appoint him to the board if it suited all parties. The move is not said to be linked to Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's £950m sale of their stakes to Clearlake Capital, which must be completed by the end of the year. Meanwhile, Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss remains a significant minority stakeholder at Stamford Bridge. The investment is also not part of a funding round, according to senior sources, and is not intended to dilute Clearlake Capital's control. However, other interested parties are said to have approached them about investing since Boehly and Walter agreed a deal to leave. Former quarterback Brady, a three-time NFL most valuable player, retired in February 2023 after 23 seasons in the NFL, having won six Super Bowl rings with the New England Patriots and one with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Following the end of his playing career he acquired a stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, while also becoming part of the ownership group of the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces. On top of that, Brady's commitments include him being a lead NFL analyst for Fox Sports. item.title: Fix Your Eyes, Fix Your Driver: The Simple Truth
item.description: Palm Desert's Anay Patel hits his driver on one at Desert Willow golf resort in Palm Desert, Calif., Thursday, March 26, 2026. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Most golfers waste money chasing driver specs when the real problem sits in their eyes. Stephen Sweeney, a PGA Tour putting coach, recently demonstrated in a lesson that correcting the setup resolves the stroke rather than the club. A Yahoo Sports report author had trouble putting this year until Sweeney identified two minor mistakes that were losing strokes. These errors happen right before the putter moves and ruin the path of the club. Sweeney observed that players often aim to the right when their eyes are positioned inside the line. “Where your eyes are right now, I tend to see if players’ eyes are inside the ball line; they tend to look out to the right,” Sweeney said. This configuration compels the putter to travel from inside to out. While such a path may suit a full swing, it destroys short putts. The fix is simple but feels weird at first. The Phone Trick That Exposes Bad Aiming The second mistake involves a putter face aligned to the right at address. Moving the eyes directly over the ball made aligning the face significantly simpler. Sweeney demonstrated a smart method involving a phone to verify aim. “Just go ahead and set up and aim your putter face,” Sweeney said. “If I go ahead and set the back of my phone to your putter face, and you come back and look down that line, you can see the face aimed on the right edge.” This visual check forces the player to see the truth about their alignment. Why Eye Position Beats New Gear Adjusting a driver loft or shaft matters less than where the eyes sit over the ball. Following only these two changes, the author felt like a different player on the greens. Confidence returned, and more putts dropped. Sweeney explained the mechanics clearly: “As the putter goes back, the putter is moving a little on the inside — but pretty square to where you aimed it.” Golf Monthly notes that Sam, an industry veteran with 15 years of experience, works on equipment advice for all levels. Drawing from his experience on the EuroPro Tour and Clutch Pro Tour, Sam possesses deep knowledge of golf equipment and what suits various golfer types. On the greens, the author felt like a new player after just these two adjustments.

item.title: When John Madden was the Raiders’ ‘Unknown Coach’
item.description: Editor’s note: This story first appeared in the November 1976 issue of SPORT magazine, written by Wells Twombly. Two months later, John Madden’s Raiders beat the Minnesota Vikings in Super Bowl XI. He went on to become a Hall of Fame coach, the defining voice of NFL broadcasts and the name on the best-selling football video game ever made. In 1976, SPORT still called him the Raiders’ “unknown coach.” Founded in 1946, eight years before Sports Illustrated, SPORT was America’s first national sports magazine. Through a partnership with SPORT magazine , The Sporting Tribune republishes a classic story and photos from the magazine’s archive each month. Who's That Guy Standing Next To The Oakland Raiders? IT'S THEIR UNKNOWN COACH, JOHN MADDEN.... By Wells Twombly When you consider the man's distinctive physical appearance and his joyous, flamboyant personality, it is all the more amazing that so few people have heard of John Madden of the Oakland Raiders. He is almost impossible to avoid, stomping the sidelines on an autumn after-noon, his large face flaming red, shouting and accusing as if someone was about to burn his house and slaughter his family. And he is the most successful unknown coach in the world. Madden simply does not register on the average person's mental screen. Try this simple test on your friends. Back them up against the bar after a long day's work and ask them to identify the only coach who ever won 70 games his first seven years in the National Football League. Or ask: Who has coached six division champions in the past seven years? Or: Who has produced more winning streaks of five games or better than any other active coach? John Madden, at age 40, has accomplished more sooner and received less credit for it than any other coach or manager you can name. All Madden does is win games. But the one game he doesn't win is the Super Bowl — and he works for Al Davis, a club owner so overpowering that he blots out the sun. So John Madden remains an individual waiting to be discovered. "Right off, I'd say that Madden is one of the finest young coaches around," says Paul Brown of the Cincinnati Bengals. "Rarely does he go into a game with only one way to beat you. Sometimes he has three, four or five. The man is a real thinker. He's a real intellectual." Madden has been described by one of his former players, defensive tackle Tom Keating, as "sweaty, like an Irish bartender on a milltown Saturday night." Photographers have won prizes taking his picture during games. One such picture leaps out at you from the wall of the lounge at the Pro Football Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio. Madden's mouth is spread wide in anger. His freckles are blazing like militant polka dots. His massive fingers point toward a distant official who has committed some nameless sin. Yet after games John Madden is invariably in breathless good humor. He grabs a can of his favorite soft drink and entertains the press with remarks that sound as if they were handed to him by

item.title: Trump FCC declares California isn't allowed to enforce phone service rules
item.description: The Federal Communications Commission ordered California to stop enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort (COLR) rules against AT&T, setting up another battle between the Trump administration and California over the state's right to enforce its own telecom laws and regulations. AT&T's status as a Carrier of Last Resort in California requires it to offer telephone service to any potential customer in its territory. AT&T wants to stop offering basic phone service to new customers and discontinue service for 184,000 residential customers and 15,000 business customers on June 1, 2027. The order released today granted AT&T's request to preempt state rules, following up on the FCC's previous approval of AT&T's petition to discontinue service. AT&T had tried to achieve the same result in court, but a federal judge rejected its request to override California's rules in July. Read full article Comments

item.title: SpaceX's Starshield troubles in Ukraine could threaten its broader military business
item.description: The representative in the US House expected to chair the House Intelligence Committee in January, Jim Himes (D-Conn.), has threatened to withhold support for funding government-owned systems from SpaceX amid the ongoing inquiry into the use of Starshield in Ukraine. "SpaceX's potentially unilateral modification of a U.S. Government contract, combined with its lack of responsiveness to congressional oversight, calls into question every contract the U.S. Government has with SpaceX," Himes wrote in a letter to SpaceX founder Elon Musk on Friday. CNN first reported the letter's existence. The network also reported that Himes sent a classified communication to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton with a similar message that it would be difficult for Congress to authorize funding for systems with SpaceX as the primary vendor. item.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
item.description: Google's flagship search experience is evolving into an AI experience with stunning speed. Even time-tested elements of search are getting AI makeovers, and the latest to get this treatment is the search homepage on Google.com. A redesign that's been in testing for the last few weeks is now official, bringing easier access to AI chats and dropping the dedicated search button entirely. Google search VP Robby Stein confirmed on X that Google is deploying the new desktop search page after a successful test. The page will now have a few more buttons under the search bar, all connected to AI features. There's an image generation button, one for analyzing files, and one for brainstorming with Gemini. The "I'm Feeling Lucky" button remains, but the Google Search button that used to sit next to it is gone. The search button has obviously been a part of Google's search page forever. However, it wasn't in a very convenient location in the modern interface. When you begin typing a query, the autocomplete suggestions cover that button. You have to click out of the text field to access the button, which is an extra step compared to simply mashing the Enter key to run your search. Read full article Comments

item.title: Meta reconsiders 2030 net-zero goal amid record emissions from AI data centers
item.description: Meta’s executives are rethinking the company’s original goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030. That revelation in Meta’s latest sustainability report comes as the company reported a record percentage increase in greenhouse gas emissions that exceeds any other Big Tech competitor racing to build new AI data centers. The company’s 2026 sustainability report claims that “our long-term ambitions haven’t changed, but our operating environment has,” according to an introduction from Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net zero and sustainability at Meta. In the November 19, 2026, report, they attributed the changing conditions and the need for a rethink to how “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” “We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones—including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets—so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” Peterson and Swedeen wrote in the report. item.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
item.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. item.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
item.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. All three financial firms attributed the compromises to a third-party provider, and while nothing in the stolen files name the vendor, the timing matches up with a Qubole supply-chain campaign disclosed earlier this month by Wiz, working with Google's Mandiant incident responders and AI data security company Sentra. item.title: What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental?
item.description: Bernhard Riemann set out a problem mathematicians have been trying solve for more than a century The Granger Collection/Alamy The cadence of prime numbers has a pattern; it isn’t simply chaos. Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. These numbers are complex – so each is actually a pair of numbers, one called real and one called imaginary – and when they are plugged into the Riemann zeta function, the function spits out zero. Confusingly, these numbers that result in a zero from the function are called “non-trivial zeros”. Riemann discovered that summing over a sequence of these complex numbers allowed him to predict the distribution of primes up to a certain high number. Effectively, he came upon a formula that could make sense of primes’ seemingly random appearances among numbers. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 20, 1998: Russia launches 1st module of International Space Station as construction begins on the largest human-built structure in orbit
item.description: null On Nov. 20, 1998, the first piece of the International Space Station launched into orbit. The 42,000-pound module is called Zarya, and it's about the size of a tour bus. Zarya launched on board a Russian Proton rocket . Two weeks later, NASA's STS-88 shuttle mission aboard Endeavour brought the Unity module into space. The STS-88 astronauts connected the two modules in orbit. Zarya was built by the Russians, but it was paid for by the United States. NASA contracted a Russian company to build it for half the price of what the American company Lockheed Martin would have charged. These days, Zarya is mainly used for storage and for external fuel tanks. The module also has docking ports for Russian Progress cargo ships and Soyuz spacecraft that carry crews to and from the space station. Today, the I nternational Space Station is about the size of a football field and typically hosts up to seven crewmembers. But back in 1998, it was a pretty tight squeeze. A Russian Proton rocket launches the core Zarya module of the International Space Station (left), which can be seen in orbit (right) during the first mission to the station in 1998. (Image credit: NASA/Roscosmos) Why it mattered As of this writing, the International Space Station is 28 years old, and has seen steady rotating crews of astronauts since the year 2000 (for 26 years and counting). It is a marvel of space engineering, but every engineering marvel begins the same: with the first piece. And that is what the Zarya module is: The foundation of the International Space Station. Zarya, also known as the Functional Cargo Block (or Russian acronym FGB), is the core module of the space station around which every other module was attached. It weighed 42,600 pounds at launch and is just aver 41 feet long and 13.5 feet wide. Inside, it boasts a total habitable volume of 1,650 cubic feet. The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA The Zarya and Unity modules are connecting in orbit to build the International Space Station. NASA NASA paid $220 million for Zarya's construction at the Krunichev State Research and Production Space Center in Moscow, with work beginning in 1994 and ending in 1998. The module is a central hub based on the success of Russia's Salyut space station designs , with two solar arrays for power and 16 external tanks to store propellant. While NASA's space shuttle Endeavour was the first to meet Zarya (and attach NASA's core Unity connecting module to it), it wasn't until Russia'z Zvezda service launched in 2000 and docked with Zarya's aft that the fledgling space station was large enough to accomodate its first three-person crew, Expedition 1. item.title: Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal
item.description: A former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF) and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Babachir Lawal, has reiterated that the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will win the 2027 general election, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the 2023 presidential poll will not be repeated. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, Lawal predicted that Obi would emerge victorious, expressing the belief that the political dynamics of the next election would be different from those of 2023. ﻿ He also questioned the outcome of the 2023 presidential election, arguing that there should have been a runoff as Obi got the highest number of votes, a development he believes would have changed the political calculations surrounding the contest. “Peter got the majority of votes; he didn’t get the spread. Bola Tinubu got the spread and came second. There should have been a runoff in that election,” he maintained. The former SGF further projected that Obi would win Kogi, Benue and Plateau states, while defeating former Vice President Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in his home state of Adamawa. “I give it to you that Peter didn’t have more spread. This time, Peter will get the spread in Nigeria. “Atiku will come third in Adamawa State this time around,” he added. On the ADC candidate’s chances in the forthcoming election, Lawal argued that the former vice president would not have sufficient ethnic support to secure the presidency. Comparing the NDC ticket with those of other political parties, he described it as a better option. Lawal also disclosed that the party’s campaign strategy would prioritise town hall meetings, which he considers a more effective means of engaging voters. He said Nigerians would look in the direction of Obi due to his character and competence. “First of all, he is incorruptible. Second, he is detribalised. Third, he is a businessman that understands market forces. And fourth, he is a man who sticks to his words,” the NDC chieftain added. Asked whether the former Anambra State governor made any promises to him, the former SGF said, “No, he doesn’t need to”. The 72-year-old said he would go back to his 4,000 hectares of farmland where he produces cash crops and livestock, and watch Nigeria grow. Asked whether he does not want to partake in Obi’s government if he wins, Babachir said, “I’m 72 years old. I have a 40-year-old son. What is wrong if Peter says, ‘I’m going to make you Minister of Agric,’ and I say Peter, instead, give my son Minister of Agric. Is that wrong? In those days when we were young, that’s how things were done.” The post Peter Obi Will Win 2027 Election, What Happened In 2023 Won’t Repeat Itself — Babachir Lawal appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5%
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips to Lows Not Seen Since 2024, Nasdaq Plunges 5% The bitcoin price slid to near $58,300 on Friday afternoon, down about 6.2% over the past 24 hours, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a deepening selloff in chip and artificial intelligence stocks sent the Nasdaq down about 5% and pushed bitcoin just under its summer low. Bitcoin broke below $60,000 late Friday morning, a few hours after this morning’s report had it near $61,500. Over the past 24 hours, the bitcoin price has traded between $57,655 and $62,562, a drop of about $3,880. Bitcoin is down about 25% in November, on pace for its worst month since June 2022. Chip stocks drag Wall Street lower Selling on Wall Street sped up through the afternoon. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5% in late trading and the S&P 500 dropped about 3.5%. Yahoo Finance said the Nasdaq was on pace to close negative for the year, while the S&P 500 was poised to close in correction territory. Chipmakers led the drop. Nvidia (NVDA) fell about 12.5% to near $128, and AMD, Broadcom and Micron also posted double-digit losses. Gold futures dropped nearly 5%. Treasury yields fell as traders rotated into bonds and defensive sectors such as consumer staples and healthcare, Reuters reported. Anthropic (ANT) fell nearly 12% to around $86 on its first full day of trading, leaving it just above its $83 IPO price. The stock had closed its Thursday debut at $97.17 after raising $81.3 billion in the largest IPO of all time, CNBC reported. Liquidations and outflows weigh on the bitcoin price Leveraged traders were forced out as the bitcoin price broke support. About $1.53 billion in crypto bets were wiped out over 24 hours, with long positions making up $1.4 billion of that total. Bitcoin alone accounted for around $540 million, while ether fell more than 8% to around $1,600. Bitcoin funds have been sellers, too. Investors have pulled roughly $3.5 billion from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs so far this month, including $582 million on Thursday. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest one-day outflow on record. Rate worries are adding pressure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent pushed back Friday on calls for a half-point Federal Reserve hike in December. Traders still saw a more than 98% chance of a quarter-point increase, and some strategists warned that further hikes could deepen the selloff. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop looks driven more by the AI stock selloff than by problems inside crypto. Bitcoin has increasingly traded alongside other growth assets that depend on easy money, he said. The dip to $57,655 briefly took bitcoin just under its summer low near $57,700. It is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, its longest losing streak since 2022.
